sections.html:
Drive about 25 miles west from Portland through the Tualatin Valley and you reach Forest Grove, the first city incorporated in Washington County, in 1872. It spreads over about six square miles at an elevation near 190 feet. The county seat is Hillsboro, and the county had 600,372 residents in 2020.

Residents numbered 26,225 in the 2020 Census, compared with 21,083 in 2010. Of 9,356 housing units, 3.7 percent were vacant, and owners occupy 59.5 percent of homes. Median age is 35.3. Many people commute to Portland-area jobs, using Oregon Route 8 or Oregon Route 47.

Forest Grove has two historic districts, the Clark Historic District and Painter's Woods, along with 12 individually listed properties on the National Register of Historic Places. The Clark district spans 18 blocks and includes homes dating to 1854.

Houses in or near these areas often keep original windows, aging wiring and older plumbing. Buyers ask what was updated, so collect permits and receipts for electrical, plumbing and window work. An owner of a historic property should talk to the city before planning big exterior changes.

Summers are warm and dry in this Mediterranean climate, and 46.72 inches of precipitation a year across about 146 days with measurable rain. Snow averages just 2.7 inches. Heat and cold still spike now and then, with a record high of 113 degrees and a record low of minus 12.

Damp is the main enemy of older houses here. Roofs, siding, gutters and crawl spaces take the brunt, and inspectors check them first. Repair what you can and be ready to explain what you cannot. Ask the inspector or a contractor for a written estimate if a big repair is in question.

sections.h2: Electric service from Forest Grove Light & Power
sections.html:
Electricity comes from Forest Grove Light & Power, a city-owned utility founded in 1895 and the third-oldest municipal electric utility in Oregon. About 90 percent of its power comes from the Bonneville Power Administration, and the rest from two hydroelectric projects in Grant County, Washington.

To stop or transfer service before closing, call 503-992-3250 on a weekday between 7:30 am and 4:30 pm, or visit the office at 1818 B Street. The utility also offers net metering for residential solar, efficiency rebates and EV charging locations, which a buyer may like to hear about.

Students in Forest Grove, Gales Creek, Dilley and part of Cornelius attend the Forest Grove School District. Pacific University and Tuality Forest Grove Hospital are both inside the city.

TriMet and the Yamhill County Transit Area run buses, and Ride Connection's free GroveLink service covers parts of the city. Many residents drive to jobs in Hillsboro, where Intel has its largest local presence, and Nike's headquarters is also in the county.

sections.h2: Farmland, orchards and the rural edge
sections.html:
Most of Washington County lies in the Tualatin Valley, with the Tualatin River running through it. Farming, lumber, manufacturing and food processing all remain part of the economy. The fertile plain around Forest Grove drew farmers early, and orchards and vineyards still shape the land west of Hillsboro.

If your property sits on the outskirts, expect buyers to ask about well and septic systems, access roads and neighboring farm activity. A rural edge is a selling point for some buyers and a drawback for others, so describe it plainly.

Selling in this county brings a real property transfer tax: one dollar for every thousand dollars of the sale price, set by Chapter 3.04 of the county code. Certain transfers can file for an exemption, and the county posts separate applications for deeds in lieu of foreclosure and for transfers a court orders.

Whether the buyer or the seller covers the charge is a matter for your sale terms. Have the title or escrow company show you the line on your settlement statement before you sign.

Tax statements go in the mail by October 25. You choose between one payment and three.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount
Full amountNovember 153 percent
Two-thirdsNovember 152 percent
Three installmentsNovember 15, February 15, May 15Interest if paid late

Late payments accrue interest at 1.333 percent per month.

A bill under $40 cannot be split into installments. Measure 50 passed in 1997 and replaced Measure 47. On a sale, the title company lists whatever is unpaid, and that amount comes out of your proceeds at closing.

A tax balance is not a barrier to selling. The title search finds it, escrow pays it from the sale proceeds, and you receive what is left. Request the payoff figure early so the number does not surprise you.

If the mortgage is behind too, say so at the start. Both payoffs appear on one settlement statement, which means nothing stays open once the deed is recorded. A fixed closing date also gives you something to plan the move around.

sections.h2: What a Forest Grove seller must disclose
sections.html:
Oregon law, ORS 105.464, has you deliver a signed disclosure statement to every buyer who makes a written offer on covered residential property. The questions touch title, water, sewage, structure, systems, flooding, settling and other defects.

After the form is delivered, the buyer gets five days to revoke the offer, unless that right was waived. A personal representative, trustee or conservator selling, or a bank selling after foreclosure, is excluded. Since the statement reflects your own knowledge, jot down leaks, repairs and past problems you have personally seen.

sections.h2: Preparing the house before buyers look
sections.html:
Before anyone tours, spend an afternoon walking the property with a notepad. Look up at the roofline and gutters, down at the crawl space access, and along the siding for soft spots. In a town this damp, those four places decide how an inspection goes.

Neighbors and buyers like to know what makes Forest Grove feel like home, so a line about the downtown Star Theatre, which dates from 1912, or the annual holiday light parade costs nothing and gives your listing some color. If you would rather skip repairs and showings, a cash sale is the alternative below.

sections.h2: Situations Forest Grove sellers often face
sections.html:
• Older houses where maintenance was put off.
  • Inherited homes with heirs living far away.
  • Landlords who are done managing tenants.
  • Owners dreading the county transfer tax added to other closing costs.
  • Homeowners who are behind and need a firm timeline.

A listing tends to mean cleaning, staging, showings and weeks waiting for a buyer's lender. With a cash purchase nobody is waiting on a loan, so the schedule is set by you and the title company. Washington County records the deed, and transfer tax, the tax split and any liens show up on the settlement statement.

Put a written cash offer next to what listing would cost you in repairs, commissions and months of upkeep. We buy houses in Forest Grove as they are, and you can request an offer online or by phone.

Gather your tax statement, mortgage payoff figure, and any lease or probate papers first, since they speed things along. If the utilities are in your name, schedule a final reading for the closing date.

A cash buyer will still ask about permits, a septic or well system if you have one, and anything that affects title. Answering plainly up front shortens the whole process.

faqs.q: What is the population of Forest Grove?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 26,225 residents. The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 27,252.

faqs.q: How much is the Washington County transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is one dollar per thousand dollars of the selling price, or 0.1 percent, under Chapter 3.04 of the Washington County Code.
Forest Grove Light & Power, a city-owned electric utility founded in 1895. Call 503-992-3250 for service questions.

faqs.q: When are Oregon property tax installments due?
faqs.a: November 15, February 15 and May 15, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full by November 15.

faqs.q: Is Forest Grove close to Portland?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 25 miles west of Portland in the Tualatin Valley.
